questions.title: Ball Stuck Next to the Fence
questions.question: Your ball is just on the golf course, but a fence that shows where the course ends is stopping you from taking your normal swing. Can you pick up your ball and move it without a penalty?

choices.text: No. Fences that mark the edge of the course don’t let you move your ball for free.
Yes, but only if you are playing match play.
You can move your ball but get one penalty stroke.

questions.explanation: A fence that shows where the golf course ends is called a boundary fence. You can’t get a free drop from this kind of fence, even if it is in your way.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A fence or wall that marks the very edge of the golf course.
Being allowed to move your ball to a better place without a penalty.

questions.teachingTip: Set up a toy fence and a ball. Ask your group what they would do if the fence stops their swing. Remind them this is different from things like benches or sprinklers.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids may believe they always get to move their ball if something is in their way.
They might think boundary fences are the same as other obstacles like benches or signs.

questions.title: Ball Against a Boundary Fence
questions.question: Your ball is just inside the course boundary, but an out of bounds fence prevents you making a normal swing. Can you take free relief?

choices.text: No. Boundary fences are boundary objects and there is no free relief.
Yes, but only in match play.

questions.explanation: Boundary fences are not obstructions. They define the edge of the course, so there is no free relief.
